<skill_content name="structurizr-validate-loop">
# Skill: structurizr-validate-loop

# Structurizr Validate Loop

You are checking Structurizr DSL with the Structurizr MCP server. Your
host prefixes the MCP tool names (for example `structurizr_validate`;
the in-harness server name is `structurizr`), so refer to the tools by
their own names — the `parse`, `validate`, and `inspect` tools of the
Structurizr MCP server — and call whichever prefixed variant your host
exposes.

## The mandatory loop

Every DSL result runs through this loop before it is returned:

1. **Parse.** Run the `parse` tool on the DSL text. Fix every error it
   reports and parse again.
2. **Validate until OK.** Run the `validate` tool. If it reports
   errors, fix them and re-run. Keep going until `validate` answers
   `OK` — do not move on, and do not report the model as done, before
   it does.
3. **Inspect.** Run the `inspect` tool on the validated text.
4. **Triage EVERY finding** into exactly one of the three labels:
   - **fix** — correct the DSL. Any edit after the final validate
     requires re-validating, so the fixed text re-enters the loop at
     step 2.
   - **expected under the MCP limits** — the finding is caused by a
     limit of the MCP (below), not by the model. Do not chase it.
   - **reported in the final answer** — a genuine recommendation that
     is not fixed now; state it in the final answer.

   A finding that cannot be cleared under the MCP never blocks the
   result.
5. **Return the exact text that last got `OK` from `validate`.** Never
   return text that was never validated to `OK`, and never return text
   that changed after the final validate: if anything is edited after
   the final validate, re-run `validate` (and `inspect` on the new
   text) before returning.

A DSL result that was only parsed, and not validated to `OK`, is NOT a
pass — a parsed-only or reported-only result is not a pass. This is the
same rule as the repo's own PlantUML validation chain (ADR
7a626b12-b189-4561-a51d-ffb2e9e133b4): a structure-only check is not a
pass.

## What the two tools answer

`validate` answers "will this parse into a workspace?" — it is
blocking, and its `OK` is the only green light this skill has.
`inspect` answers "does this follow C4 and Structurizr
recommendations?" — its findings are recommendations, never a failed
validate. See `references/validate-vs-inspect.md` for the side-by-side
table and the common findings with their triage.

## The MCP limits

The Structurizr MCP tools have hard limits; state them in the final
answer whenever they affect the result:

- **DSL text only, single file.** The tools work on the workspace's
  DSL text given as one input; there is no multi-file workspace.
- **`!include`, `!docs`, and `!adrs` are refused.** A DSL that uses any
  of them gets a refusal that reads like "feature … is not enabled" —
  the MCP sandbox does not enable those importers. Do not use them,
  and never "fix" a missing-documentation or missing-decisions finding
  by adding `!docs`/`!adrs`: triage that finding as expected under the
  MCP limits and report it as expected in the final answer.
- **No image rendering.** The MCP cannot produce image files (PNG/SVG).
  Its export tools emit diagram source only — PlantUML, C4-PlantUML,
  or Mermaid text. If images are requested, say so.

## When the MCP is absent

If the Structurizr MCP tools are not available in the host, validation
is not possible. State that in the final answer and never describe a
DSL result as validated — a result the tools could not check is
unvalidated, no matter how well it looks.

## Gotchas that surface in the loop

`references/dsl-gotchas.md` collects the DSL rules whose violations the
loop most often meets: declaration order (elements before the
relationships that use them), quoting, a description and a technology
on every relationship, and flat, model-wide-unique identifiers.

Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.
Note: file list is sampled.

Read file /work/.opencode/skills/structurizr-validate-loop/references/dsl-gotchas.md, lines 1-48
1: # DSL gotchas
2: 
3: The rules whose violations the validate loop most often meets, and how
4: to write the DSL so they do not. Each rule exists because breaking it
5: caused a concrete failure or an unhelpful diagram.
6: 
7: ## Declaration order
8: 
9: The DSL is parsed top to bottom. An element must be declared before any
10: relationship that references it. A forward reference fails with
11: `The destination element "x" does not exist` — the same error as a
12: typo, so check the identifier first, then the order. Declare all
13: elements first, then the relationships; put cross-container component
14: relationships (for example `spa -> authController`) after the closing
15: brace of the system that contains both containers, not inside the first
16: container.
17: 
18: ## Quoting
19: 
20: Quote every name, description, and technology. Unquoted strings with
21: spaces and unbalanced braces surface as `Unexpected tokens` / parse
22: errors in `validate`.
23: 
24: ## Relationship description and technology
25: 
26: Give every relationship both a description and a technology:
27: `a -> b "Reads orders from" "HTTPS/JSON"`.
28: 
29: - The description is a verb phrase from the source's point of view:
30:   "Reads orders from", "Publishes events to". Avoid "Uses" and "Calls".
31: - The technology answers "what would I edit or configure?":
32:   "Express Router", "TypeORM", "Kafka topic orders.v1", "PostgreSQL
33:   16" — not "JavaScript".
34: - Between components in one container, `"In-process call"` is an honest
35:   technology.
36: 
37: A missing technology is the most common inspect finding
38: (`model.relationship.technology`); a missing description is the other
39: half of the pair (`model.relationship.description`).
40: 
41: ## Flat identifiers
42: 
43: Prefer flat identifiers. Skip `!identifiers hierarchical` unless two
44: elements would otherwise share an identifier — with hierarchical
45: identifiers every reference must spell out the full path, and mistakes
46: produce the same "element does not exist" error as a typo. With flat
47: identifiers, every identifier must be unique across the whole model,
48: and flat identifiers validate on the first try more often.

1: # validate vs inspect
2: 
3: Two tools, two questions. Users who ask "is this valid?" want
4: `validate`. Users who ask "is this complete?" or "is this a good
5: model?" want `inspect`.
6: 
7: | | `validate` | `inspect` |
8: |---|---|---|
9: | Question | Will this parse into a workspace? | Does this follow C4 and Structurizr recommendations? |
10: | Output on success | `OK` | List of findings, or nothing |
11: | Output on problems | `ERROR ... at line N of workspace.dsl: <source line>` | One line per finding: `ERROR \| <rule id> \| <message>` |
12: | Blocking? | Yes. Nothing is valid until it answers `OK`. | No. Findings are recommendations. Never treat a finding list like a failed validate: a workspace can validate cleanly and have dozens of inspect findings. |
13: 
14: ## Common validate errors
15: 
16: | Message | Cause | Fix |
17: |---|---|---|
18: | `The destination element "x" does not exist` | Typo, missing element, or relationship declared before the element | Check the identifier; move the relationship below the element's definition |
19: | `The source element "x" does not exist` | Same as above, for the left side | Same |
20: | `Unexpected tokens` / parse errors | Unbalanced braces or unquoted strings with spaces | Quote every name, description, and technology |
21: 
22: ## Common inspect findings
23: 
24: | Rule id | Meaning | Triage |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | `workspace.scope` | No workspace scope set | fix — add `configuration { scope softwaresystem }` (one detailed system) or `scope landscape` |
27: | `model.relationship.technology` | A relationship has no technology | fix — add a third string: `a -> b "Calls" "HTTPS/JSON"`; use `"In-process call"` between components |
28: | `model.relationship.description` | A relationship has no description | fix — add a verb phrase: `"Reads orders from"` |
29: | `model.softwaresystem.documentation` | A system with containers has no docs | expected under the MCP limits — the MCP refuses `!docs`; do not add it. Report the finding as expected in the final answer |
30: | `model.softwaresystem.decisions` | A system with containers has no ADRs | expected under the MCP limits — the MCP refuses `!adrs`; do not add it. Report the finding as expected in the final answer |
31: | `views.view.key` / `views.view.layout` | A view has an auto-generated key | fix — give every view an explicit key: `container system "Containers" { ... }` |
32: | `model.*.description` | An element has no description | fix — add the description string after the name |
33: 
34: Report inspect findings grouped by rule id with counts, and say which
35: ones are worth fixing. Do not describe the workspace as broken because
36: of them.
